title: Parallel Tempering Molecular Dynamics (PTMD) for Cu90
action: Run PTMD simulations for a Cu90 cluster using the Gupta potential in LAMMPS. Use the replica temperatures exactly as provided in the paper's Table S4 for Cu90 (37 replicas from 300 K to 800 K). Equilibrate for ~0.5 μs, then sample configurations every 125 ps after each swap attempt for a total sampling time of ~1–2 μs. Collect all local minima visited during the production run (distinct minima differing by at least 0.05 meV or different structure type).
description: PTMD simulation produces high-temperature ensembles, the caloric curve, and a pool of local minima for HSA analysis.

title: Harmonic Superposition Approximation (HSA) analysis
action: From the PTMD-sampled local minima, select those up to an energy cutoff of 1.2 eV above the global minimum (target ~10,000 distinct minima). Classify each minimum into a motif (Ih, Dh, fcc, twin, mix, amorphous) using Common Neighbor Analysis (CNA). For each minimum, compute normal-mode frequencies via diagonalization of the Hessian, then evaluate the HSA probability p_i(T) using Eq. (3) of the paper, summing to obtain temperature-dependent motif probabilities up to 300 K.
description: HSA provides low-temperature motif probabilities (0–300 K) that are later stitched with PTMD results.

title: Stitched structural distribution output
action: Combine the HSA motif probabilities (valid up to 300 K) and the PTMD motif probabilities (valid above 300 K) into a single continuous curve. At the stitching temperature 300 K, use the HSA values or an average if there is a small jump. Extract the probabilities of the six motifs (Ih, Dh, fcc, twin, mix, amorphous) at the exact temperatures 300, 400, 500, 600, and 609 K. Save these as a CSV file with columns Temperature, Motif, Probability.
description: The stitched structural distribution CSV contains the equilibrium motif probabilities at the requested temperatures.
output_schema: Columns: Temperature (float), Motif (string, one of Ih, Dh, fcc, twin, mix, amorphous), Probability (float between 0 and 1). Rows: 5 temperatures x 6 motifs = 30 rows.

title: Melting point determination
action: From the PTMD caloric curve (heat capacity C_V vs temperature), identify the temperature at which C_V reaches its maximum. Output this temperature (in Kelvin) to a single text file.
description: The melting point is defined as the peak of the heat capacity curve.
output_schema: A single floating-point number in Kelvin (e.g., 609.0).
